findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false; the feature-flag check is dead, inverted code
findings.body: The new function `enableSqlExpressions` computes `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`, then returns `false` on every path (both inside the `if enabled` branch and at the final return). The flag therefore has no effect at all — which matches the PR's intent of hard-disabling SQL expressions for CVE-2024-9264, but the code is written as if it were a real flag check, with a variable named `enabled` holding the inverse of the flag state. This is a maintenance hazard: a future reader can easily misread it as flag-gated behavior, or 'simplify' it to `return enabled`, which would invert the flag (feature on when flag is off, off when flag is on). If the hard disable is intentional, the function should be reduced to an explicit `return false` (or the gate inlined) with a comment stating that SQL expressions are deliberately disabled for CVE-2024-9264, so the behavior cannot be accidentally changed.

findings.title: No regression test pins the disabled-SQL-expression behavior
findings.body: This security fix changes behavior in two places (ReadQuery now rejects `type: sql` queries, and the `sql.DB` stub makes `sql.TablesList`/`NewSQLCommand` always fail), but the PR adds no test asserting either behavior. There is nothing preventing a future refactor — e.g., someone 'implementing' the stub `DB` in pkg/expr/sql/db.go by reintroducing a DuckDB dependency — from silently re-enabling the vulnerable code path. A small test that ReadQuery returns an error for a SQL expression query, and that NewSQLCommand fails, would lock in the mitigation. The PR also does not touch any existing tests covering the SQL expression parser/command paths, so the impact of the always-erroring stub on the existing pkg/expr test suite should be verified before merge.

findings.title: Stub DB has no comment explaining it intentionally disables SQL evaluation
findings.body: The newly added `DB` type replaces the DuckDB-backed implementation with methods that all return `errors.New("not implemented")`, but neither the type, the methods, nor `NewInMemoryDB` carry any comment explaining that this is a deliberate security mitigation for CVE-2024-9264 (RCE/LFI via DuckDB) rather than an unfinished feature. Without that context, the stub looks like work-in-progress code that a contributor might helpfully 'finish' by re-adding go-duck, reintroducing the vulnerability. A short package/type comment referencing the CVE and stating that SQL expression evaluation must stay disabled would prevent that.
